correctness.rationale: The alternating bracket model is free by the two-generator class-three universal property, and each invertible degree-one block A has all six lower-degree parameters available. With δ=det A, the diagonal blocks are A, δ, δA. Once A²=I and C(A+δI)=0, the alternating 2×2 identity gives E=−JCᵀ and AE=−E, so the only remaining constraint is DA+δAD+EC=0. Conjugating A by a change of generators preserves the fiber count. In odd characteristic the fibers over I, −I and a split reflection have sizes 1, q² and q³; the last type has q(q+1) linear blocks by choosing ordered distinct eigenlines. In characteristic two the identity block forces C=0 with arbitrary D, while a nontrivial unipotent gives C=(0,h) and the constraints e=0, j=d+h². Such unipotents correspond to an image=kernel line and a nonzero quotient-to-line map, giving q²−1 blocks. Thus both polynomials, including the identity, follow over every finite field. A separate direct 5×5 matrix enumeration over F₂, F₃ and F₄ gave 40, 334 and 1216, with the expected linear-block fiber sizes. This is corroboration, not the general proof.
residual_risks: Finite replay covers only q=2,3,4; the general result depends on the block and field argument.

value.rationale: The algebra is the smallest natural two-generator free Lie example with a degree-three lift layer. Its square-one census gives an exact count of maps from C₂ into this automorphism group (and of elements of exact order two after subtracting one), relevant to finite automorphism-group and involution calculations. The modular lift obstruction shows why the answer is not obtained by simply transferring the odd-characteristic census or the abelianization count.
residual_risks: This does not classify automorphism conjugacy or cover other free ranks or nilpotency classes.
